Development on August 9 focused on stabilizing the Eliza framework through modular UI migrations, critical runtime bug fixes, and significant CI/CD pipeline improvements. The team successfully restored Gmail functionality and addressed core orchestration issues, while ongoing efforts remain centered on resolving cloud infrastructure latency and agent provisioning stability.

🚨 Needs Attention

  • elizaos/eliza#16961 (Cloud Warm Pool): Requires input on digest-aware rollout status and daemon-owned capacity guards to resolve image-drift issues.
  • elizaos/eliza#18049 (Auth Latency): Investigation into multi-second provider lookup spikes needs further analysis to reduce bootstrap latency for onboarding.

✅ Completed Work

Core Runtime & Agent Orchestration

  • Fixed planner loop failures to ensure tool results are preserved even during mid-turn interruptions (elizaos/eliza#18180).
  • Enhanced agent engagement by suppressing meta-narration and improving routing gates (elizaos/eliza#18174, elizaos/eliza#18177).
  • Improved task management by reaping stuck tasks and preventing internal instructions from leaking into chat (elizaos/eliza#18118, elizaos/eliza#18164).

UI & Connector Migration

  • Migrated settings to a modular, connector-based architecture with dedicated detail pages (elizaos/eliza#18175).
  • Enabled in-process token redemption to resolve app-host pairing issues (elizaos/eliza#18178).
  • Refined browser workspace UX by cleaning up chat composer controls (elizaos/eliza#18124).

CI/CD & Google Workspace Stability

  • Restored Gmail sending capabilities with new security fail-safes against header injection (elizaos/eliza#18112, elizaos/eliza#18121).
  • Stabilized CI test lanes by serializing dependencies and bounding worker teardowns (elizaos/eliza#18193, elizaos/eliza#18136).
